title: Bidirectional A* in Sapporo: Meet in the Middle!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* slice through a real street-like grid from Susukino, expanding from both start and goal. It finds a fast route by combining heuristic guidance with graph search from two directions until the frontiers connect.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ Route-finding, but smarter: **Bidirectional A*** from **Susukino → the destination** in Sapporo.

🔎 **How it works (deep but practical):**
In graph terms, we treat the street network as a weighted graph (intersections = nodes, roads = edges). **Bidirectional A*** runs two coordinated A* searches: one forward from the start and one backward from the goal, each guided by an admissible heuristic (e.g., estimated travel cost based on geographic distance). When the two frontiers meet, we stitch the partial paths into a complete route—often cutting search effort dramatically versus single-direction A*.

🗺️ **Real street-map flavor:**
Because the “graph” is derived from real map geometry (grid/graph abstraction of roads), corner constraints, edge weights, and heuristic distance all influence expansion order—so you can literally see algorithm strategy play out on a map-like layout.

🚗💡 In **Sapporo (Susukino)**, we visualize **graph search** using **Bidirectional A***—a smarter pathfinding approach that expands from both the start and the goal.
